competition: Swiss Biology Olympiad (SBO) — 1st and 2nd rounds (English translation)

problems.problem:
Cells are the basic unit of all known living organisms. They contain specialised structures that carry out various functions in the cell. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The endoplasmic reticulum has a rough and a smooth part.

B. Mitochondria are involved in the production of ATP.

C. DNA has the 3D structure of a double helix.

D. The cytoskeleton is responsible for detoxifying the cell.

Membranes consist of a lipid bilayer. Lipids are characterised by having large hydrophobic parts and are therefore poorly soluble in water. On the basis of this information, determine for the following molecules whether they can move freely through a membrane (true) or not (false).

A. Negatively charged proteins.

B. Water molecules.

C. Lipid-soluble oestrogen.

D. DNA fragments.

The thyroid hormone T3 increases the metabolism of the human body. The amount of T3 in our body is regulated, among other things, by feedback mechanisms. Using the figure, indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-3-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Hypothalamus produziert TRH = hypothalamus produces TRH; Hypophyse produziert TSH = pituitary gland produces TSH; Schilddrüse produziert T3 = thyroid gland produces T3; Hemmung = inhibition; Stimulierung = stimulation.

A. In the absence of T3, the production of TRH is increased.

B. TSH stimulates the production of T3.

C. T3 inhibits the production of TRH and TSH.

D. TRH inhibits the production of T3.

Indicate whether the following features belong to a prokaryotic cell (true) or not (false).

A. Nucleus

B. Membrane-bound organelles

C. Centrosome

D. Cell membrane

Indicate for each of the following statements about mitochondria whether it is true or false.

A. Proteins produced in mitochondria are secreted into the cytoplasm of the cell.

B. If the mitochondria of a cell lose functionality, this can lead to a shortage of ATP.

C. In plant cells, chloroplasts take over the function of mitochondria.

D. Under aerobic conditions, the majority of a cell's ATP is formed in the cytoplasm.

Cells possess numerous enzymes that catalyse various chemical reactions. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Enzymes lower the activation energy of a reaction.

B. Enzymes shift the equilibrium of a reaction towards the products.

C. To catalyse a reaction, the enzyme must bind to at least one of the reactants.

D. Doubling the concentration of an enzyme leads to a doubling of the yield of the reaction.

The conversion of mRNA into a peptide is called translation. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Several specialised RNAs are involved in translation.

B. During translation, the primary structure of the finished peptide is formed.

C. Translation in the cell takes place inside the nucleus.

D. Every four nucleotides of the mRNA correspond to one amino acid in the finished peptide.

Indicate for each of the following statements about DNA replication whether it is true or false.

A. Newly synthesised DNA must be joined by a ligase into an uninterrupted DNA strand.

B. The DNA strands formed during DNA replication are joined by helicase into a new helix.

C. In DNA replication, the entire complementary strand is first synthesised from RNA and then replaced by DNA.

D. DNA polymerase starts from single-stranded DNA.

Cells multiply by a single cell splitting into two daughter cells. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. During cell division, the spindle apparatuses ensure that the cell organelles are distributed evenly between the two daughter cells.

B. Most prokaryotes have the ability to divide an unlimited number of times.

C. During cell division, plant cells usually constrict in the middle, which separates the daughter cells from each other.

D. During the division of human cells, the chromosomes line up in the equatorial plane in order to be distributed evenly to the daughter cells.

You sequence the same section in a coding region of a gene of two individuals of the species Arabidopsis thaliana. You obtain the sequences AAGTTCCGT in individual 1 and AAGTCCGT in individual 2. Which of the following terms best describes the observed mutation from individual 1 to 2?

A. Silent mutation

B. Frameshift mutation

C. Nonsense mutation

D. Addition

Which statement about viruses is true?

A. Viruses have neither DNA nor RNA.

B. Viruses cannot reproduce on their own.

C. Viruses infect only animal cells.

D. All viruses have a nucleus.

Atoms and molecules form different bonds with one another. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. When table salt dissolves in water, van der Waals forces act between the salt ions and the water molecules.

B. Hydrogen bonds contribute to the stability of secondary structure elements in proteins.

C. pH influences protein structure by enabling or preventing ionic bonds.

D. All stable compounds occurring in nature satisfy the octet/duet rule.

Many vascular plants have specialised tissues for the transport of substances. A distinction is made between xylem and phloem. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. In most trees, phloem and xylem are arranged in rings.

B. In the xylem, substances are transported from the root to the leaves.

C. Sugar is transported within the plant via the phloem.

D. The phloem consists of dead cells.

Indicate for each of the following statements about photosynthesis whether it is true or false.

A. The molecules of the light reaction are located on the thylakoid membrane.

B. CO₂ is consumed in the dark reaction.

C. Plants absorb light energy with photosystems.

D. Plants are green because they mainly absorb light with wavelengths in the green range.

Similarly to animals, plants have hormones that control various functions. One example is auxin, which promotes root growth at low concentrations and shoot growth at high concentrations. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Auxin is present in increased concentration during shoot formation.

B. Auxin can control the direction of root growth.

C. If auxin is deposited on the left side of the shoot axis, the shoot axis bends to the right.

D. A genetic defect that reduces the production of auxin can lead to excessive root growth.

Indicate for each of the following molecules whether it is involved in photosynthesis (true) or not (false).

A. Cellulose

B. Chlorophyll

C. Carbon dioxide

D. NADPH

Indicate for each of the following cell organelles whether it occurs in both animal and plant cells (true) or not (false).

A. Chloroplasts

B. Vacuole

C. Golgi apparatus

D. Mitochondria

Indicate for each of the following statements about the reproduction and structure of flowering plants whether it is true or false.

A. Pollen is collected in the ovary.

B. Pollen grains form a pollen tube on the stigma.

C. Pollen is produced by the stamens.

D. Petals often serve to attract insects.

Indicate for each of the following molecules whether it is released by the leaves on a warm, sunny day with moist soil (true) or not (false).

A. O₂

B. H₂O

C. N₂

D. CO₂

Indicate for each of the following statements about plant stem cells whether it is true or false.

A. They have the potential to form a completely new plant.

B. They have a different genome from the parenchyma cells of the shoot.

C. They have a rigid cell wall.

D. They occur in the shoot tip and the root tip.

Water potential is a measure of the energy of a body of water. The main influences on water potential are mechanical pressure, osmotic pressure and gravity. Water always flows from higher to lower potential. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. If a cell is placed in a solution with a lower water potential, it dries out.

B. During active photosynthesis, the water potential of plant leaves is lower than the water potential of the roots.

C. Highly concentrated solutions have a lower potential than solutions of low concentration.

D. The roots of a plant generally have a lower water potential than their surroundings.

Some plants enter into a symbiosis with soil fungi in which they exchange substances. Which of the following substances is given by the plant to the fungus?

A. Nitrogen

B. Water

C. Iron

D. Glucose

Mammals have a four-chambered heart, which allows them to avoid mixing of oxygen-poor and oxygen-rich blood. Indicate for each of the following statements about the functioning of the mammalian heart whether it is true or false.

A. Oxygen-rich blood reaches the heart via the pulmonary veins.

B. During the filling of the ventricles, the atrioventricular valves are open.

C. When the ventricles contract, the blood is pumped into the arteries.

D. Oxygen-poor blood is found in the left half of the heart.

Animals that adapt their salt concentration to that of their surroundings are called osmoconformers. Animals that keep their salt concentration stable are called osmoregulators. Indicate for each of the following animal species whether they are osmoconformers (true) or not (false).

A. Tuna

B. Mussels

C. Shrimps

D. Dolphins

Indicate for each of the following statements about respiration whether it is true or false.

A. A respiratory organ works better the larger its surface area.

B. Gills use the co-current principle to take up oxygen from the water more efficiently.

C. We have to inhale oxygen so that we can run the respiratory chain efficiently.

D. Insects need lungs for oxygen exchange.

Indicate for each of the following statements about energy metabolism in animals whether it is true or false:

A. The most important energy-carrier molecule in an animal cell is AMP.

B. The combustion of sugar provides the organism with energy.

C. If environmental conditions are harsh, an animal can shut down its metabolism.

D. Surplus energy can be stored in the form of fat for longer periods.

Indicate for each of the following statements about reproduction whether it is true or false:

A. Animals that produce sperm are called males.

B. In sexual reproduction, the offspring is called a clone.

C. In animals that live only on land, external fertilisation is often found.

D. Some animals change their sex in the course of their life.

Indicate for each of the following statements about the human kidney whether it is true or false.

A. White blood cells mature in the kidney.

B. The kidney eliminates toxins, drugs and their metabolites.

C. The kidney secretes hormones.

D. Carbohydrates are digested in the kidney.

Indicate for each of the following processes whether it is involved in synaptic signal transmission between a nerve cell and a skeletal muscle cell (true) or not (false).

A. The neural crest cells migrate along the neural plate

B. An electrical stimulus is generated by the sinoatrial node

C. Calcium influx causes vesicles to fuse with the cell membrane

D. Neurotransmitters open the ion channels of another cell

Indicate for each of the following statements about human axons whether it is true or false.

A. The nerve cell receives signals from other cells via the axon.

B. Axons in the central nervous system are supplied with oxygen directly by capillaries.

C. A single axon can be part of both the central and the peripheral nervous system at the same time.

D. In the unmyelinated axon, signal conduction is saltatory.

Indicate for each of the following components of the immune system whether it belongs to the innate immune response (true) or not (false).

A. Plasma cells

B. Mechanical barriers

C. Macrophages

D. Antibodies

Indicate for each of the following statements about the pancreas whether it is true or false.

A. The digestive enzymes produced by the pancreas are only activated in the small intestine.

B. The pancreas is both an exocrine and an endocrine gland.

C. During digestion, the pancreas secretes an alkaline secretion.

D. Insulin is produced in the pancreas.

It is a hot summer's day and you walk, sweating, to a fan. Which mechanisms contribute substantially to your cooling (true) or not (false)?

A. Convection

B. Vasoconstriction

C. Heat radiation

D. Evaporation

Thyroxines (hormones of the thyroid gland) act on the production of the hormone TSH via a negative feedback loop. Which of the following graphs best represents the correlation between thyroxines and TSH?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-34-fig1.png

Indicate for each of the following animals whether it has an open circulatory system (true) or not (false).

A. Drosophila melanogaster (fruit fly)

B. Lumbricus terrestris (earthworm)

C. Hyla arborea (European tree frog)

D. Salmo trutta (trout)

In addition to the blood circulation, humans have a further vascular system: the lymphatic system. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The lymphatic system serves to recover substances that diffuse through the capillary walls.

B. The human spleen is closely connected with the lymphatic system.

C. The lymphatic system is an open circulatory system.

D. New immune cells are formed in the lymph nodes.

Indicate for each of the following statements about osmosis whether it is true or false.

A. Osmotic pressure can transport substances against gravity.

B. Osmosis takes place when there are differences in the concentrations of dissolved substances.

C. Without countermeasures, a (hypotonic) fish in the sea dries out because of osmosis.

D. Osmosis is only possible across a semipermeable membrane.

Ivan Petrovich Pavlov rang a bell every time he fed his dogs. After a certain time, the dogs also began to drool when he rang the bell without giving them food. This is an example of:

A. Operant conditioning

B. Habituation

C. Reciprocity

D. Classical conditioning

A bonobo (Pan paniscus) gives a banana to another individual in its group. This behaviour is:

A. Sexual selection

B. Egoism

C. Food mutualism

D. Altruism

After mating, the female cuckoo (Cuculus canorus) looks for an unattended nest of another bird species, lays her egg in it and flies away. The incubation of the egg and the care of the chick are taken over by the "adoptive parents", who do not notice that it is not their own offspring. What type of interspecific relationship is this?

A. Commensalism

B. Mutualism

C. Parasitism

D. Competition

Indicate for each of the following behaviours whether it is innate (true) or not (false).

A. The ability of a parrot to utter certain words

B. A dog sitting down at the command "Sit"

C. The burying of nuts in autumn by squirrels

D. The feeding of cheeping chicks by bird parents

Traits of different animal species are called homologies if they have a common origin. Traits are called analogies if they are similar but arose independently of each other. Indicate for each of the following examples whether it is a homology (true) or an analogy (false).

A. Beak of a squid and of a bird

B. Ulna and radius of a bird and of a crocodile

C. Streamlined body of a dolphin and of a penguin

D. Wings of a bat and of a bird

Which of the following mechanisms is most likely responsible for the origin of an analogous trait?

A. Adaptive radiation

B. Genetic drift

C. Bottleneck effect

D. Selection

You cross two homozygous four o'clock plants (Mirabilis jalapa). One has red flowers and the other has white flowers. All offspring have pink flowers. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The pink flowers are a case of intermediate inheritance.

B. The pink flowers are heterozygous.

C. The offspring of a pink and a white flower will be half white and half pink.

D. If you cross two of the pink offspring, their offspring will again all be pink.

The father of a family has blood group AB and the mother has blood group A. Indicate for each of the following blood groups whether it is possible in the children (true) or not (false).

A. A

B. B

C. AB

D. O

Indicate for each of the following effects whether it occurs in ideal populations (true) or not (false).

A. Migration

B. Genetic drift

C. Sexual selection

D. Inbreeding

Two maize strains are planted on different soils that differ in their nitrogen content. All individuals of a strain are genetically identical. The norm of reaction indicates how strongly the environment affects the phenotype. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-47-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Ertrag (kg/ha) = yield (kg/ha); Stickstoffanreicherung (kg/ha) = nitrogen enrichment (kg/ha); Maisstamm 1 = maize strain 1; Maisstamm 2 = maize strain 2.

A. The amount of enriched nitrogen depends only on the genotype.

B. Maize strain 2 has the larger norm of reaction than maize strain 1.

C. The environment (here: the nitrogen content of the soil) affects all genotypes equally strongly.

D. In a trait with a large norm of reaction, genetically identical individuals also have the same phenotype.

Mice that live on dark rock have darker fur than mice that live in light-coloured grass. To which effect is this due?

A. Disruptive selection

B. Stabilising selection

C. Frequency-dependent selection

D. Directional selection

You observe a male peafowl (Pavo cristatus) that has a strikingly long tail, which prevents the male from flying and thus makes it more vulnerable to attacks by predators. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The reason for the occurrence of males with long tails is sexual selection.

B. Peacocks with shorter tails generally have a higher fitness.

C. Females that mate with males that have a longer tail generally have a lower fitness.

D. It is to be expected that peahens prefer males that have a long tail.

The pedigree shows the inheritance of a disease. Circles denote women, squares men. Affected individuals are marked in black. How is the disease inherited?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-51-fig1.png

A. X-linked recessive

B. Y-linked

C. Mitochondrial

D. Autosomal dominant

Huntington's chorea is an autosomal dominant inherited disease. The disease is caused by an above-average number of repeats of the three bases CAG in the gene that codes for the protein huntingtin. As a result, huntingtin can still carry out its normal function, but it has a toxic effect on the cells because of the high number of glutamine residues. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. This type of mutation is called a missense mutation.

B. If both parents are ill, all their children are also affected by the disease.

C. The reading frame in the mutated variant of the gene is shifted.

D. The denatured huntingtin of ill people is longer than that of healthy people.

A silent mutation is a mutation in a coding section of DNA that has no effect on the amino acid sequence of the protein. Indicate for each of the following mutations whether it can be a silent mutation (true) or not (false).

A. Insertion of 3 base pairs

B. Inversion of 4 base pairs

C. Deletion of 2 base pairs

D. Point mutation

The absence of the tail (allele A) in cats is inherited dominantly. The litter of two tailless cats (genotype Aa) consists of one third kittens with a tail and two thirds kittens without a tail. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The litter of two cats with tails consists only of kittens with tails.

B. The frequency of allele A has decreased in the kittens compared with the parental generation.

C. The kittens with tails have genotype aa.

D. Cats with genotype AA are not viable.

In a paternity test, DNA samples are taken from the putative father and the child, and various genetic markers are compared. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. A paternity test is more informative if the genotype of the mother is also known.

B. A paternity test must give the same genotype for the child and the biological father.

C. A paternity test can exclude paternity, but cannot confirm it 100%.

D. A paternity test becomes more reliable the more genetic markers are compared.

Which of the following answers classifies humans (Homo Sapiens) correctly:

A. Metazoa: Protostomia: Mollusca: Cephalopoda

B. Metazoa: Deuterostomia: Amniota: Eureptilia

C. Chordata: Vertebrata: Tetrapoda: Mammalia

D. Chordata: Vertebrata: Amniota: Sauropsida

Indicate for each of the following statements about systematics whether it is true or false:

A. Analogous structures are a clear sign of relatedness.

B. There is only one way to define the term species.

C. Homologies and analogies arise through evolution.

D. Biological relationships are determined only on the basis of physical traits.

Indicate for each of the following plant groups whether it belongs to the seed plants (Spermatophyta) (true) or not (false).

A. Ferns (Polypodiopsida)

B. Magnolias (Magnoliidae)

C. Conifers (Pinophyta)

D. Mosses (Bryophyta)

The figure shows the temperature–performance curves of four species (A, B, C, D). The dotted line shows the current temperature in their common habitat. Which of the four species will lose the most productivity under a general rise in temperature?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-59-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Leistung = performance; Temperatur = temperature.

Strangler figs are climbing plants that use tropical tree species as supporting structures. After some time they encircle the trees so tightly that the trees die. Which of the following words best describes the relationship of the strangler figs to the trees?

A. Obligate mutualism

B. Parasitism

C. Predator–prey relationship

D. Symbiosis

Indicate for each of the following statements about ecological niches whether it is true or false.

A. The realised ecological niche is generally larger than the fundamental ecological niche.

B. The same species can occupy different niches in different habitats.

C. If many predators are present, the fundamental and realised ecological niches of the prey are usually the same.

D. The fundamental ecological niche of a species changes markedly when a competing species becomes extinct.

You observe a forest in which foxes and rabbits live. At present there are equal numbers of individuals of both species. You look at the course of the population sizes over a long period. Which of the following scenarios is the most likely for the course of the population size of the foxes?

A. Exponential growth

B. Fluctuation around an equilibrium

C. Linear growth

D. Steady decline

You observe two different insect species A and B, both of which have a similar, strikingly colourful coloration. Species A is poisonous, but species B is harmless. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. The similar coloration is an advantage for species B.

B. Such similar colorations often occur in habitats with high pressure from predators.

C. For the warning coloration to work, the poison of species A must necessarily be lethal.

D. The similarity of the colorations is based on sexual selection.

Insects, skunks and foxes live on an isolated island. After the golden eagle is introduced to the island in 1960, the food web looks like this:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-64-fig1.png

The sightings of eagles, skunks and foxes are counted and look like this:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-64-fig2.png

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. If all the insects on the island die out, this has no effect on the eagle population.

B. The skunk population increases because fewer skunks are eaten by foxes.

C. Foxes and skunks compete for their food.

D. The introduction of the eagle is a possible cause of the decline of the foxes.

Some years ago, seeds of the Norway spruce Picea abies were sown on alpine meadows. After ten years, the number of trees was measured. What limits the spread of Picea abies to higher altitudes in nature?

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2021-1-65-fig1.png

A. Dispersal strategy

B. Unsuitable habitat

C. Infertility of the seeds

D. Competition with other tree species

What is the name of this molecule?

A. Cytidine monophosphate

B. Cyclic guanosine monophosphate

C. Tetrasodium diphosphate

D. Adenosine triphosphate

Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. Glycine is the simplest amino acid; it has no side chain. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2022-1-2-fig1.png

A. In proteins, the amino acids are linked via their side chains.

B. The chemical properties of amino acids differ because of their side chains.

C. Glycine is chiral.

D. Glycine can form disulfide bridges.

Some cells have a flagellum, a whip-like structure that serves for locomotion. Indicate for each of the following cell types whether it can have a flagellum (true) or not (false).

A. White blood cell

B. Sperm cell

C. Muscle cell

D. Bacterium

Indicate for each of the following statements about DNA whether it is true or false.

A. DNA contains uracil.

B. DNA contains sugar.

C. DNA contains phosphate.

D. DNA contains amino acids.

Indicate for each of the following statements about fungi whether it is true or false.

A. Fungi belong to the vascular plants.

B. The cell wall of fungal cells consists of lignin.

C. Fungi can be multicellular.

D. Lichens are a symbiosis between fungi and algae.

Look at the figure of a biomembrane and indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2022-1-6-fig1.png

A. A is a protein.

B. B is hydrophobic.

C. C is a DNA chain.

D. D is a phospholipid.

Consider the following reaction:

$$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \Rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O}$$

Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. Energy is released in the reaction.

B. At room temperature the reaction proceeds spontaneously.

C. The reactant $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}$ can be glucose.

D. In the reaction, oxygen is oxidised.

The polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is a biochemical method to amplify DNA in vitro. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. In each temperature cycle the DNA is doubled.

B. Even small amounts of DNA can be amplified by PCR.

C. DNA synthesis takes place at 95 °C.

D. Magnesium ions supply the energy for the reaction.

Protein biosynthesis at the ribosomes differs between prokaryotes and eukaryotes. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

A. In prokaryotes, most mRNAs code for more than one protein.

B. In eukaryotes, mRNA is exported from the nucleus after transcription.

C. In prokaryotes, mRNA can be translated as soon as it has been synthesised.

D. In eukaryotes, each mRNA codes for three proteins.

RNA is chemically less stable than DNA. Indicate for each of the following possibilities whether it is a reason for this (true) or not (false).

A. RNA strands form more bonds than DNA strands.

B. RNA contains ribose instead of deoxyribose.

C. RNA consists of larger molecules than DNA.

D. Unlike DNA, RNA is often present as a single strand.

The figure shows part of a signalling pathway. Apoptosis is controlled cell death. Indicate for each of the following statements whether it is true or false.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Eisatopon/biology-olympiads-bank/main/images/sbo-2022-1-11-fig1.png

Figure labels (German → English): Apoptose = apoptosis.

A. The concentration of AKT depends on MAP3K.

B. Apoptosis can be suppressed without AKT.
